segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: In the moment I went with unit count — Order A first — partly because that's our default rule when picking between two rush jobs.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The planner considered the tighter packaging slot and selected Order A using an explicit production rule; the generation specification treats this as plausible domain reasoning, not an intentional bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I decided to just treat Line 3 as available overflow capacity if Line 1 or Line 2 fell behind, and moved on to the next issue.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is the planned Bounded Rationality instance: under concurrent demands, the planner accepted the first workable assessment and did not check the readily available Order C dependency before committing Line 3.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I decided to provisionally build the buffer units into the Order B plan rather than wait, because waiting with no ETA on a callback risked losing time I couldn't get back.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The planner made a reversible provisional plan under uncertain QA timing and explicitly planned to adjust if QA flagged an issue; this is treated as reasonable operational planning.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Overtime plus talking to the carrier directly gave me a shot at getting the full order out with minimal disruption, even shipping a few minutes past official cutoff.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The planner explicitly weighed overtime, partial shipment, and renegotiation, then made a documented cost and customer-service trade-off; the generation specification does not mark this as biased.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Line 3 intermittent alarm and overflow capacity decision
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Acceptance of the first satisfactory option (operator's informal reassurance) under multi-threaded time pressure, foregoing a readily available check of Order C's dependency on Line 3 output, because exhaustive verification exceeded practical time and attentional capacity in the moment.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Automation complacency is a related monitoring/verification construct, but it is not an established alias for the hidden Bounded Rationality target. The benchmark requires the label-plus-mechanism scorecard to treat this as a wrong-label case.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding explicitly describes accepting the operator's familiar alarm assessment under concurrent task pressure and failing to check the available Order C dependency before committing Line 3. This fully matches the hidden mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted interview evidence is verbatim and correctly localized. The retrospective reflection is used as supporting context, while the at-time decision evidence is also present.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The RAG detects the correct decision episode at moderate confidence and raises no identified findings on the negative segments.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: Candidate inclusion preserves detection of the positive episode but adds two false alarms on negative segments; the third candidate duplicates the already detected positive episode.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, the RAG detects the one positive decision segment with no identified false alarms: segment hit rate, precision, recall, and F1 are all 1.0.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: The strict instance scorecard records 0 true positives because the RAG uses automation complacency instead of the hidden Bounded Rationality label; the correct episode and mechanism are therefore a wrong-label FP/FN case.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: The mechanism-first scorecard records 1 true positive, 0 false negatives, and 0 false positives at high_and_moderate, showing that the RAG captured the hidden reasoning mechanism despite the taxonomy mismatch.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: Two candidates are useful abstentions on negative segments, while the third is a plausible but duplicate near-miss for the already identified Line 3 episode. Including candidates adds two segment false alarms and no new true positive.
main_failure_modes: Neighboring-label substitution: automation complacency was used instead of the hidden Bounded Rationality label.
Candidate over-generation on two otherwise negative decision episodes.
A duplicate candidate was emitted for an already identified positive episode.
main_strengths: Correctly localized the positive Line 3 episode.
Captured the hidden mechanism of accepting a workable option under concurrent pressure without checking an available dependency.
Quoted the interview accurately and appropriately treated hindsight as supporting context rather than sole proof.
Correctly left the QA buffer episode unclassified.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run is a strong mechanism-level detection with a strict taxonomy miss. At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold it has perfect segment-level detection, but zero strict label-plus-mechanism instance F1 and perfect mechanism-first instance F1. Candidate inclusion reduces precision through false alarms without improving recall.
